sources.fullCitation: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique. “Jean Féline.” Musée SACEM, Les créateurs. Lyricist, screenwriter and dialogue writer, born 30 October 1908 in Saumur, died 17 January 1945 in Paris; admitted to SACEM as author on 1 May 1935.
sources.title: Jean Féline — Musée SACEM creator record
sources.creator: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique
sources.repository: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique / Musée SACEM
sources.researchNote: The membership register gives 30 October 1908 as the date of birth, agreeing with the Paris death certificate of January 1945 and superseding the tentative year 1912 carried by the BnF heading. Admission as an author on 1 May 1935 marks the start of his professional song writing, shortly before the first songs published under his name.

sources.shortCitation: ‘Le gala de la Charité maternelle,’ Excelsior, 25 June 1932, p. 2
sources.fullCitation: ‘Le gala de la Charité maternelle.’ Excelsior (Paris), 25 June 1932, p. 2. Stage photograph captioned ‘Une scène de “La Grande-Duchesse et le garçon d’étage”’ and identifying, from left to right, Cécile Sorel, Jean Féline and A. Fauchier-Magnan. Bibliothèque nationale de France / RetroNews.
sources.title: Jean Féline at the Charité maternelle benefit — Excelsior, 1932
sources.creator: Photographer unidentified
sources.researchNote: The printed caption unambiguously identifies the seated man as Jean Féline. Identification with the lyricist and screenwriter born in 1908 is probable rather than certain: his age is compatible, he was active in the Paris theatre milieu by 1932, and a second captioned photograph in Comœdia of 13 March 1933 again names a Jean Féline among the society performers of ‘Sa Flambée’. The latter photograph is credited to Studio Piaz and is used only as corroborating identity evidence, not reproduced here.

media.title: Jean Féline, identified in Excelsior — benefit performance, 1932
media.description: Faithful portrait crop from a stage photograph published in Excelsior on 25 June 1932. The printed caption identifies the seated man between Cécile Sorel and A. Fauchier-Magnan as Jean Féline. His identification with the lyricist and screenwriter Jean Féline is probable, supported by his age and documented activity in the Paris theatre milieu, but is not treated as certain.
media.altText: Sepia halftone press photograph of a young man identified as Jean Féline, seated in evening dress and shown in profile during a benefit performance.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The photograph was published without a photographer or agency credit in the French newspaper Excelsior in 1932 and is treated as an anonymous work whose French term expired more than seventy years after publication. Its original French term had already expired before the United States URAA restoration date, so no restored U.S. copyright is claimed for the photograph.
media.publicCaption: A man identified by Excelsior as Jean Féline during a benefit performance at the Théâtre de la Michodière in 1932; identification with the lyricist and screenwriter is probable.
media.publicCreditLine: Photographer unidentified; Excelsior, 25 June 1932, p. 2, detail. Bibliothèque nationale de France / RetroNews.
